scope.offset_semantics: start inclusive, end exclusive; offsets obtained through offsets_for_times, falling back to the captured end offset when no timestamp offset exists

read_only_controls.retained_record_scope: Only metadata samples for the three named real calls to our own Leader; no raw Kafka values, headers, request/response bodies, credentials, or other users' records are saved

caller_record_checks.limits: Results apply only to records in the captured topic offset ranges; they do not prove caller records were never emitted, published to another topic/broker, delayed beyond the window, or stored elsewhere

observations.group_sample_semantics: Each sample below is the first observed Kafka record in that task/method group. count is the actual group total. This report does not expand unsaved records into invented individual samples.

documented_rules_and_source_findings.finding: The live platform documentation requires Access correlationId to be taskId and counts one call through bilateral taskId matching
documented_rules_and_source_findings.verification: Read directly from the live platform documentation during this investigation

documented_rules_and_source_findings.finding: Official SDK 2.2.0 caller emitter uses correlation_id=command.sessionId; this is a possible incompatibility with the documented taskId rule, not evidence of DingDang's actual deployed caller output
Official Monitor topology materialized view counts the callee perspective and is not the website's documented bilateral matched-stats algorithm
Our callee emitter uses the genuine taskId and passes no trace parameters; missing uploaded trace metadata does not prove that the caller omitted the incoming traceparent HTTP header

conclusion: The captured amp.access window contains genuine task-correlated callee records for all three named DingDang tasks, but no corresponding caller-side record was found. This window lacks the public evidence needed for the documented bilateral match.
limitations: No conclusion is made about caller records outside the captured offset ranges or about all platform history
Kafka timestamp offsets define the captured range; a delayed or differently timestamped caller upload can fall outside it
Caller records with both incorrect participant identities and unrelated correlation identifiers may evade the targeted checks
The actual deployed DingDang caller correlation_id and trace fields remain unobserved; SDK defaults are not proof of deployed behavior

The website matched-stats implementation was not available in the inspected public v2.2.0 tree; additional matching conditions, ingestion state, aliases, exclusions, and deduplication behavior are unverified
Kafka delivery and schema validity do not by themselves prove ingestion into the platform matching store or a completed bilateral match
The callee collector does not retain HTTP traceparent, so it cannot establish whether incoming DingDang requests carried trace context
